title: Wiring
note: One USB-C port for charging and data: VBUS charges the cell through the TP4056, and D+ and D- go to the Pico's USB test pads. Two 1N5822 diodes share the load: the MT3608 runs from whichever of VBUS and the cell is higher, so with USB in the cell only charges. A third 1N5822 joins the MT3608 (set to about 5.2 V) to the Pico's VSYS, so nothing can push power back into a computer. D2, D3, the resistors, C1, Q1, the buzzer and the DS18B20 sit on the wiring board; D1 is soldered onto the MT3608.

groups.label: Load sharing (diode OR)
groups.note: With USB in, VBUS through D2 (about 4.6 V) is above the cell through D3 (at most about 3.85 V), so D3 is off and the cell only charges; the TP4056 then ends the charge properly. With USB out, the cell runs the MT3608 through D3.

components.name: USB-C breakout
components.note: The only USB port on the unit. CC1 and CC2 each have a 5.1 k resistor to GND on the board, so a USB-C charger supplies 5 V; SBU1 and SBU2 are not used. It sits in a pocket in the front wall, its mouth 0.4 mm from the outside, held down by the USB clamp.

components.name: TP4056
components.note: 1 A single-cell charger with protection (DW01 + 8205A), on the floor behind the USB-C board, held at its corners. Its own USB-C port is not used: power comes in on IN+ and IN-. IN- and OUT- are joined on the board.

components.name: 1S BMS
components.note: Mantech 210454 protection strip, on the cell. A second layer of protection in series with the TP4056's own; it can be left out.
One 18650 cell in its holder, glued to the floor, the BMS strip on top.

components.name: 1N5822
components.note: The cell's side of the diode OR, on the wiring board.

components.name: 1N5822
components.note: USB's side of the diode OR, on the wiring board.

components.name: MT3608
components.note: Boost converter: set its trimmer for about 5.2 V out before connecting the Pico. It runs from 2 V up, so the diode's drop costs little of the cell.

components.name: 1N5822
components.note: Joins the MT3608 to VSYS, soldered by its anode lead into the MT3608's VOUT+ hole (open it to 1.4 mm); the VSYS wire goes on its cathode lead. The Pico's own diode joins VBUS to VSYS, so whichever is higher runs it, and nothing flows back into the USB port.

components.name: Pico 2 W
components.note: On its side behind the LED stick. USB data reaches it on test pads TP3 (D+) and TP2 (D-) on its underside, so its micro-USB port is not used. It can tell USB is in from VBUS sense (WL_GPIO2 on the Pico 2 W). GP26 (ADC0) reads the cell through the R4/R5 divider: volts = reading x 3.3 / 4095 x 2.

components.name: WS2812 x8
components.note: Eight LEDs in the lid's windows; up to about 480 mA at full white. Its data comes straight from the 3.3 V GPIO, which works at this supply in practice.

components.name: 47R
components.note: Limits the button's LED to a few mA from the 3.3 V GPIO; check against the LED's rating.

components.name: TSD-1166
components.note: Push button with a white LED ring, through the back wall. The switch reads on GP3 with the internal pull-up.

components.name: 1k
components.note: The transistor's base resistor.

components.name: BC337
components.note: Switches the buzzer: a GPIO cannot give its 30 mA.

components.name: Buzzer 5V
components.note: Active 5 V buzzer, 30 mA, on the wiring board at the front.

components.name: DS18B20
components.note: On the wiring board at the front, behind the vents: it measures the air inside the box; one-wire on GP6.

components.name: 4k7
components.note: The one-wire bus's pull-up.

components.name: 100k
components.note: The divider's top: from the protected cell (BAT).

components.name: 100k
components.note: The divider's bottom: halves the cell's 3.0 to 4.2 V to 1.5 to 2.1 V, under the ADC's 3.3 V. The pair draws about 20 uA from the cell all the time.

components.name: 100n
components.note: Across R5: a low-impedance source for the ADC's sampling, so the 50 k divider reads true; it also smooths the reading.

components.name: 330R
components.note: In the LED stick's data line: damps ringing on the wire and protects the first LED's input. Best near the stick; on the wiring board the wire is short.

nets.name: VBUS
nets.note: 5 V from the USB-C port. It charges the cell, feeds the Pico (through its own diode) and, through D2, the MT3608.

nets.name: GND
nets.note: The protected side of the TP4056 (IN- and OUT-, joined on its board). Never join it to B- or the cell's negative.

nets.name: PACK-
nets.note: Through the BMS strip's MOSFETs. Leave the strip out and the cell's negative goes straight to the TP4056's B-.

nets.name: SYS_IN
nets.note: The MT3608's input: the higher of VBUS and the cell, less a diode's drop.

nets.name: BOOST
nets.note: About 5.2 V, set on the MT3608.

nets.name: VSYS
nets.note: About 4.8 V after the diode: the Pico, the LEDs and the buzzer.

nets.name: LED_DIN_R
nets.note: After the 330 R, into the stick's first LED.

nets.name: RING
nets.note: The button's LED ring: high is on, PWM to dim.

nets.name: VBAT_SENSE
nets.note: Half the cell's voltage, on GP26 (ADC0). With USB in it reads the charging voltage, so judge the charge state with USB out (or the TP4056 idle).
